Members had concluded the Chapter 61A purchase of 360 Flat Hill Road could not be pieced together in time; a funding gap remained beyond a donor's pledge.
The chair will send a summary email to the select board and talk further with the donor and the buyer's attorney.
The committee heard a Forest Legacy presentation, a cost-share federal program needing a local match, and held the item over to the next meeting.
A resident suggested a dedicated fund so the town can act on short Chapter 61A deadlines; the town-owned property list review was continued.

why_it_matters: The recommendation points toward the town not buying 360 Flat Hill Road, so that land could pass to a private buyer and leave town ownership; the select board still has to act on the committee's advice.

Chapter 61A deadlines are short, and without money already set aside the town may be unable to buy land in time; a dedicated acquisition fund would need town meeting approval to spend, so residents could be asked to vote on it.

what_happened.line: The Open Space Committee voted to recommend to the selectmen a 200-foot setback from Mopus Brook at 250 Howard Street.
It voted to recommend two rear parcels, on Mopus Road and West Townsend Road, go to the care and control of the Conservation Commission.
It voted to ask that it be empowered to examine all undesignated municipal lands and develop a process, and to approve the 671 West Street request while deferring the others.
The committee recommended that town boards seek a gift of part of the Bright Farms property for trail access; the recording does not make the vote outcome audible.
The economic development designee was deferred, and the next meeting was set for October 13 at 6 p.m.

why_it_matters: The setback and the land transfers decide how much land along Mopus Brook and in other town-owned parcels is kept as conservation or trail land rather than left open to other uses.
These were recommendations only: the selectmen and other boards still decide, and any town land conveyance or transfer may need a Town Meeting vote.
The Marshall Park master plan is meant to be paid mostly by grants and earmarks, so the local tax cost is expected to be small, but that depends on the grants being awarded.
watch_next: Next Open Space Committee meeting, October 13 at 6 p.m. (dates may change with Zoom availability).
The selectmen's response to the 250 Howard Street setback recommendation, and the copy of the earlier town meeting article on 671 West Street.

what_happened.line: The Open Space Committee voted to recommend that the town pursue its right of first refusal on the 250 Howard Street land.
The committee voted to encourage the planning board and conservation commission to secure trail connectivity or an easement between two town parcels near the proposed greenhouse parcel.
The recommendation is to be forwarded to the chair and then to the board of selectmen ahead of their September 8th meeting.
Exercising the right would need an appropriation by town meeting, as explained in the discussion of the Chapter 61B withdrawal.
Members nominated Paula as vice chairperson, and meetings were set for the third Tuesday of each month at 6 p.m.

why_it_matters: If the town exercises the right of first refusal on 250 Howard Street, town meeting would be asked to vote an appropriation, which would draw on the town budget, mostly taxes.

Chapter 61 programs lower an owner's property taxes in exchange for the town's right of first refusal, so the vote touches both land the town could keep as open space and the revenue it gives up under the program.
watch_next: The board of selectmen meeting on September 8th, where the recommendation is due to be passed on.
The next committee meeting, which is to take up the list of town-owned parcels for possible conservation or parks control and candidates for the economic development committee seat.
